prompt: Today, more and more people use robots to do tasks at home and at work. Do you think it is a positive or negative development? Why?
essay:
In recent years, there has been an ongoing debate regarding whether more and more people use robots to do tasks at home and in the workplace.  A group of individuals believes that using machines offers a lot of advantages. Conversely, others argue that it is not a viable solution. Therefore, ahead of my opinion, both views will be discussed further.

Examining the former opinion, the primary argument that supporters would put forward is that the advantages of high-tech , in the same way as the seniors, offer a multitude of benefits that extend far beyond mere convenience and flexibility. Using machines can serve as a means of saving time and increasing efficiency. This is because individuals can clean up settings while working, cooking or doing anything. A pivotal aspect to consider is that individuals can have more time for loved ones, friends, and recharge battery after a hectic day.  It can be a great way to drive innovation in various industries and improve productivity for companies. Therefore, automation helps businesses create new products, improve processes, and discover more efficient ways of working.

On the contrary, those in favour of the latter opinion have their own arguments. In contrast, the negative effects of using automated machines in the workplace or at home should not be underestimated, as they can not only negatively affect employees who are at risk of losing their jobs but also increase dependence on electronic devices.  A pivotal aspect to consider is that employees facing excessive pressure may experience stress, burnout, and anxiety regarding their work, income, and future. For instance, unemployment is currently rising, while communication problems and the increasing cost of food and other goods are creating additional pressure on employees. This can lead to poor work-life balance and reduced quality of life. Moreover, reliance on high-tech has led to a reduced physical fitness and a sedentary lifestyle. To illustrate, people who frequently rely on advanced technology may experience a decline in cognitive function and critical-thinking skills.

To conclude and offer my position, there are convincing arguments both for and against using cutting-edge technology at home and at work. It is a double-edged sword, offering immense opportunities for learning while also presenting significant challenges. However, I certainly favour the former.
